title: Quadratic irrational analogues of Ramanujan's series for $1/π$
summary: About 40 years ago Jonathan and Peter Borwein discovered the series identity $$ \sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{(-1)^n(6n)!}{(3n)!(n!)^3} \frac{(A+nB)}{C^{n+1/2}} = \frac{1}{12π} $$ where \begin{align*} A&=1657145277365+212175710912\sqrt{61},\cr B&=107578229802750+13773980892672\sqrt{61},\cr C&=\left(5280(236674+30303\sqrt{61})\right)^3 \end{align*} which adds roughly 25 digits of accuracy per term. They noted that if each of the quadratic irrationals $A$, $B$ and $C$ is replaced by their conjugates, that is, each number $a+b\sqrt{61}$ is changed to $a-b\sqrt{61}$, then the resulting series also…
